## What Will You Learn Today?

By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

Explain why MPI is useful for parallel computing

Compare shared-memory threads with MPI processes

Compile and launch one MPI program as multiple processes

Exchange data using MPI_Send and MPI_Recv

Scale Beyond One Machine Processes can run across multiple hosts Standard Communication Abstractions Send / Recv / Broadcast / Reduce Communication is explicit, but MPI hides low-level network details. MPI combines private process memory with portable communication across one or many machines.

# Practice: Run and Modify the Programs SHORT LAB — NOT A FORMAL ASSIGNMENT
## Task A — Hello MPI
Compile the Hello MPI program.
Run with `-n 1`, `-n 2`, and `-n 4` Record the rank and size printed by each process. Observe whether output order changes.
## Task B — Send / Recv Rank 0 sends an integer to Rank 1. Rank 1 prints the received value.
✓ Change the value and tag.
Run with at least two processes.
## Optional extension Rank 1 modifies the value and sends it back to Rank 0.
